notes: StreamDecisionBench (single community author; arXiv 2609.38612; MIT): 480 stream states in 8 scenarios and 4 families, scored with an untimed accuracy and an in-force accuracy that penalises slow answers. 30 model settings; here the decision-model settings are stored (generative references Terra/Astra/Luna "low"/"none" are listed in claims by the labels the board prints, because their versions cannot be resolved to model-catalog ids). Clef (hosted path unknown) scores 38.96% untimed vs Perplexity 70.00% and Jev 62.36%; the hosted Workers AI 2K-token state truncation (OpenRouter note) is a POSSIBLE cause and is UNVERIFIED. Hosted vs self-hosted latency rows use separate metric ids. Weak provenance: one author, one snapshot.

claims.statement: StreamDecisionBench (untimed % / in-force %): Perplexity Decider v1 27B 70.00 / 63.37; Kev-27B 72.64 / 62.15; Jev 62.36 / 58.50; Clef 38.96 / 31.39; GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API) 36.04 / 32.39; Clef Flash 21.67 / 19.89. Generative references as printed by the board: "Astra low" 99.86 untimed / 49.51 in-force (p50 2.353 s), "Terra low" 95.76 / 52.06, "Luna low" 89.93 / 45.45, "Terra none" 81.88 / 55.46, "Luna none" 43.54 / 30.87. The time budget flips the order: slow, accurate generative models lose in-force accuracy to fast decision models.
claims.implication: This is the one board where Clef trails badly; it measures evolving-stream decisions, a different task shape from classification and tool selection. Treat the Clef gap as unexplained (possible hosted truncation, unverified).
